text.p: These are the leading stories in the Albanian press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- An editorial says President Sali Berisha, who resigned on Wednesday, represents the last Albanian typical authoritarian leader.
- Thousands of people fired into the air across the country to celebrate Berisha's resignation. Once he tendered his resignation his office was looted by unknown people.
- Unlike after May 1996 elections, all western diplomats in Albania attended Wednesday's first session of the parliament which resulted from June 29 elections.
- The World Bank will help Albania once the new government is formed and new legislation passed by parliament, permanent representative Carlos Elbirt says in an interview.
- A police station in the northernmost district of Malesia e Madhe was fired on by unidentified gunmen who killed one policeman.

- The paper says the theft of 15 rockets from a garrison in Gjirokaster might have been an attempt to discredit interim defence minister Shaqir Vukaj, a northerner, so that Sabit Brokaj from south Albania can become the new defence minister.
- Democratic Party secretary-general Genc Pollo failed to address a protest to parliament as his request to take the floor was rejected.
- Greek police expelled some 1,500 Albanian emigrants on Wednesday.
- Special police units were sent to secure the customs office in Kakavije, on the Greek border.

- The international community will help the Albanian government not only to re-establish public order but also to rebuild state institutions and the country's shattered economy, OSCE special envoy Franz Vranitzky said.
